transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Communities along the U.S. Gulf Coast are making final preparations
before Hurricane Isaias arrives.
The storm is getting stronger.
It's now a 120-mile-per-hour CAT III.
As NPR's Debbie Elliott reports,
Isaias is projected to make landfall tonight or early in the morning
near the Alabama-Florida border.
Forecasters with the National Hurricane Center
say this will be a dangerous hurricane at landfall.
Local officials have ordered evacuations along some Florida panhandle beaches
and have opened shelters.
Alabama ordered tourists to leave its coast.
More than half of the offshore oil and gas production in the Gulf
has been curtailed according to the Marine Minerals Administration.
Debbie Elliott, NPR News, Crestview, Florida.
The legendary former NFL coach and player Mike Ditka has died.
A family spokesperson says Ditka died this morning surrounded by family and friends.
He was 86.
As our member, Station WBEZ, writes,
the Hall of Famer played on the Bears' 1963 NFL championship team
and coached the Bears to their only Super Bowl championship
after the 1985 season.
He is being remembered as a larger-than-life personality
beloved by a generation of Bears fans.
A new federal forecast projects record electricity use
in the U.S. this year and next,
partly driven by the growth of artificial intelligence.
And Piers Windsor-Johnson reports that rising demand
is already pushing up prices in some parts of the country.
The forecast comes from the Energy Information Administration.
AI data centers need large amounts of power
to run their computers and keep them cool.
Costa Sameras directs Carnegie Mellon University's
Scott Institute for Energy Innovation.
Places like the Mid-Atlantic where electricity demand from data centers
is rising very quickly and there's not a lot of new electricity supply.
Electricity prices are going up.
Sameras says expanding data centers can require costly power lines
and other equipment.
He says lawmakers need regulations that make those companies cover the costs.
Windsor-Johnson, NPR News.
The federal immigration agent shot and injured a man in the Bronx yesterday,
and Piers Jasmine Garris reports officials have identified the individual.
His 28-year-old Dominican National Oscar Belgao.
Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said ICE agents attempted to arrest the man
while he was in his car with a five-year-old boy believed to be his son in the back seat.
One of the agents was wearing a construction worker vest.
Seven shots were fired into the car.
The man was injured in his neck.
The child, Tisch said, is unharmed.
The Department of Homeland Security has stated that Belgao is in the U.S. without papers
and had been convicted of grand larceny.
Commissioner Tisch said he also had a pending drug case.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul and Mayor Zoran Mamdani condemned the shooting
and accused the Trump administration of, quote, "terrorizing our city."
Jasmine Garris, NPR News, New York.
This is NPR News.
Family and friends are mourning the death of Curtis Flowers.
He was a former Mississippi death row inmate who spent decades behind bars
before the Supreme Court threw out his capital conviction citing racial bias
in the jury selection of the black man's multiple trials.
One of Flowers' attorneys, Tucker Carrington, says Flowers' case was historic.
He's the only person to have been tried six times.
And ultimately, after all those years on death row, he was exonerated.
Flowers died Wednesday.
After struggling with diabetes, the cause of death has not been disclosed.
The former president of Barre College, Leon Botstein,
is now resigning from all campus-affiliated positions after coming under scrutiny
for his links to the late convicted sex offender, Jeffrey Epstein.
Maryam Akhmoud of Member Station WAMC has details.
Botstein resigned after the ranking Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee
called for a federal criminal investigation into his relationship with Epstein.
An email allegedly sent from the address president@var.edu to Epstein in 2014
asked if a young woman was, quote, "for me or are you keeping her for yourself?"
Five years later, Epstein was formally charged with sex trafficking.
Botstein denied sending the email.
He retired in June, but has remained on campus as a teacher and orchestral conductor.
First-year student Ingrid Larson wants Botstein removed from campus.
He needs to leave, and I think that if he doesn't,
I hope that people really show up to get him out of here.
Bard has confirmed Botstein will move out of the president's residence.
For NPR News, I'm Maryam Akhmoud in Albany.
I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News, in Washington.
Angie app.

topics.text: Hurricane Isaias strengthens to Category 3, projected to make landfall near Alabama-Florida border tonight
Legendary former NFL coach and player Mike Ditka dies at age 86
Federal forecast projects record electricity use in U.S. this year and next, driven by AI growth
ICE agent shoots and injures 28-year-old Dominican national Oscar Belgao in Bronx during arrest attempt
Curtis Flowers, exonerated Mississippi death row inmate after six trials, dies following diabetes complications
Leon Botstein resigns from all Bard College positions amid scrutiny over Jeffrey Epstein connections
